about: sha256 of the pre-push hook text that each PUBLISHED @rightkit/release writes with `rightkit-gate install-hook` into an app that has it installed, i.e. hookText("node_modules/@rightkit/release/bin/rightkit-gate.mjs"). `install-hook` refuses to overwrite a hook that differs, so the hook committed in desktop-app-template/.githooks/pre-push must be byte-identical to what the release the template pins writes, or `pnpm install` (the `prepare` script) fails in every app copied from the template. template-contract.test.mjs compares the committed hook with the digest recorded here for the pinned release; no network is needed. The entry for a release is computed from the PUBLISHED tarball, never from this tree: npm pack @rightkit/release@<version> into an empty directory, extract it, then run `GATE_MODULE=<extracted>/package/bin/rightkit-gate.mjs node --input-type=module -e "import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'; import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'; const { hookText } = await import(pathToFileURL(process.env.GATE_MODULE).href); console.log(createHash('sha256').update(hookText('node_modules/@rightkit/release/bin/rightkit-gate.mjs')).digest('hex'));"` from outside that directory (the path goes in the environment, not in argv: a gate module named in argv[1] would run as the entry point). The publish bookkeeping commit that moves registry.npm to a new @rightkit/release version adds that version's entry here; the test then requires the tree's own hookText to match it. Releases before 0.6.4 are not recorded.
